used_by: The local:env command in the root package.json.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and file location
sections.what: Brings in the libraries and sets the location of the .env file at the repo root.
sections.why: Makes clear where the generated settings go.
sections.watch_out: The header says the file must not be committed, but this script does not enforce that.

sections.name: flag
sections.title: Reading options and checking input
sections.what: Reads options from the command line, falling back to the database environment variable. Generates a password when none is given. Checks the role and the password length, and refuses to overwrite an existing file unless forced.
sections.why: Stops bad or accidental changes before anything is written.
sections.watch_out: An option name with no value after it is read as missing, so the default is used silently.

sections.name: lines
sections.title: Building and writing the file
sections.what: Hashes the password, creates the login entry, generates a random signing secret, and writes the file. It then prints a summary and any generated password.
sections.why: Hashing means the file never contains the plain password.
sections.watch_out: Each run creates a new signing secret, so running with force will likely log out existing users.

summary: Creates the local .env file with a random signing secret and one login account. It uses a password the developer provides, or generates one.
purpose: Gives a developer a working local configuration in one command.
why: The header describes the purpose. The login password is stored only as a bcrypt hash, so the plain password is not saved in the file.
how: Reads the options given on the command line. Generates a password if none is supplied. Checks the role and the minimum password length, and refuses to overwrite an existing file unless forced. Hashes the password and builds the login entry. Writes the file with owner-only permissions, prints a summary, and shows any generated password once.
inputs: Command options: database address, username, role, password, and a force flag. The database address can also come from DATABASE_URL.
outputs: A .env file at the repo root, console messages, and a generated password shown once if one was created.
risks: A generated password appears in the terminal and may remain in the scroll history. The file contains the login list, so a leaked .env exposes the hashes. A username that contains a single quote could break the file. Re-running with force creates a new signing secret, which will likely invalidate existing logins.
debug: If it refuses to run, delete .env or add the force flag. If login fails, check the username and role inside AUTH_USERS, then re-run with force. If the database address is not set, edit .env.
